source_metadata.title: Ask, Condition or Abstain: Reinforcement Learning for Missing-Premise Reasoning
source_metadata.design: AI/ML training and benchmark study of reinforcement learning for missing-premise reasoning

source_consistency_findings: The abstract, introductory text, and MPB diagnostic Table 7 describe six perturbation types, while Table 8 in the arXiv HTML representation enumerates seven construction-method rows because it includes both qualifier removal and qualifier disruption. This was not silently reconciled.
The evaluator-agreement appendix reports approximately 98% and 95% agreement but does not report the sampled response counts in the inspected text.
extraction_limitations: Atoms are grounded in arXiv:2608.16554v1 as accessed on 2026-08-19 and remain marked needs_review pending human verification.

The web PDF parser exposed the 15-page text, but repeated PDF screenshot requests failed with an arXiv cache-miss error. Figure and table coverage was therefore reconciled against the arXiv HTML representation and parsed PDF text rather than rendered page images.
No raw source bytes were available through the web/PDF tool path, so input_document_hash is null rather than invented.
The paper states that code, MPB, and training data are released, but the inspected article text did not expose a directly extractable repository URL.
Repeated textual restatements were not duplicated as atoms; the set prioritizes independently reviewable methods, main benchmark results, ablations, evaluator checks, limitations, and conclusions.
schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated benchmark-configuration, model-evaluation, or evaluator-agreement atom kinds; these claims are represented with method, outcome_definition, quantitative_result, qualitative_result, or other supported kinds.
